description: The production Vercel WAF configuration for Coding Journal. Rules are listed in the order they should be published; the first match wins. Stage them with `node scripts/print-firewall-commands.mjs`, review with `vercel firewall diff`, then publish.

rules.name: Block exploit probes
rules.why: Scanners cost invocations on paths the product does not serve. Nothing legitimate requests them.

rules.name: Rate limit authentication
rules.why: Sign-in and the OAuth callback are the only unauthenticated write surface. A per-client ceiling blunts credential stuffing without touching a real sign-in.

rules.name: Rate limit journal actions
rules.why: Server actions post to the page path. The application budgets these per user as well; this bounds a client that is not signed in at all.

rules.name: Rate limit GitHub installation callbacks
rules.why: The install and setup callbacks write installation state. GitHub itself never needs more than a handful per minute.

rules.name: Rate limit GitHub webhooks
rules.why: Deliveries are signature-verified before any database work, so this is a volume ceiling only. It is deliberately generous: GitHub delivers from shared egress addresses, and a dropped delivery is a lost event.

rules.name: Rate limit operations endpoints
rules.why: The cron dispatches and the health view are bearer-authorized. This bounds guessing at the secret.

rules.name: Per-client request ceiling
rules.why: The backstop under every rule above: no single client should be able to drive the whole product's invocation bill. Sits last so a more specific rule matches first.
